profile.headline: Missouri's governor is landing $10-15 billion data centers, while voters in Festus threw out the council that approved one and protesters want a statewide moratorium.

sections.text: Gov. Mike Kehoe has promoted data centers as economic development and hosted a Governor's AI and Data Center Forum at Missouri S&T on June 18, 2026. In June 2026 he responded to calls for a special session on data centers, but none has been called.

In May 2026 Google announced a $15 billion data center near New Florence in Montgomery County, the largest single investment in state history. In June 2026 AWS announced a $10 billion data center in the same county, with completion tentatively in 2032. Festus approved a $6 billion project in March 2026.

In April 2026 Festus voters removed incumbent council members after the council approved the $6 billion data center; a judge dismissed a suit over a rejected recall vote in September. About 200 protesters filled the Capitol on September 16, 2026 asking for a statewide moratorium on hyperscale construction and an end to tax incentives. A Benton County moratorium is being fought in court.

The University of Missouri launched the AI Education, Research and Infrastructure Center (AERI) on May 27, 2026 to connect AI research across campus and build computing infrastructure. Washington University started a campus "+AI" initiative in March 2026.

Sen. Josh Hawley is among the Senate's most active AI critics. In a June 2026 op-ed he listed his bills, including the GUARD Act (criminal penalties for AI that sexually solicits children or encourages self-harm), the AI Risk Evaluation Act and the GRID Act, and argued data-center companies should cover their infrastructure costs. He co-sponsors Grassley's AI Whistleblower Protection Act.
